## 76c3f9d7128a

**A1 — Reproduced exact-axis/override-contract defects; audit target unchanged.** Generator SHA-256 `6ba9ab227d908ffb307ba59fff4ee80a4960838d7a990329096b6a38ef594fec`; selected canonical Racket rule hash `e1575fb1600b`.

The declared numeric axis ranges do not match their override validity gates. At seed `123`, sample index `0`, the following documented-valid values raise `ValueError`:

| Difficulty | Override | Declared valid | Actual rejection range |
|---|---|---|---|
| medium | `grid_h=8` | `8..18` | `[11,15]` |
| medium | `grid_w=18` | `8..18` | `[11,15]` |
| medium | `n_pairs=5` | `3..5` | `[3,4]` |
| easy | `n_pairs=5` | `3..5` | `[3,3]` |
| hard | `n_pairs=3` | `3..5` | `[4,5]` |

These are independently feasible shapes/counts; difficulty changes the random defaults but currently also narrows the advertised override domain. [probe.json](checks/audit/76c3f9d7128a/probe.json) retains all five exact messages and source declarations.

The helpful `palette_kind` and `texture` choices are also inert. Keeping seed `123`, index `0`, medium difficulty, and `n_pairs=3`, changing either field from `default` to each of `warm`, `cool`, and `varied` produces the same input in **6/6 comparisons**. Source inspection confirms that neither helpful field is consumed; only three degenerate `texture` values receive a special branch. Every compared input passes `self_check` with `[]`. No claim of a broad ordinary-sampling census is made.

The baseline ordinary input is in [input.json](checks/audit/76c3f9d7128a/input.json). The supported public command executed the selected canonical authority on it and returned a valid output with no reference error ([racket.json](checks/audit/76c3f9d7128a/racket.json)). [counterexample.json](checks/audit/76c3f9d7128a/counterexample.json) combines the exact source/rule identity, seed/index/overrides, input, self-check membership, output and reproduction command. `rival_output` is `null` and differing cells are empty because the primary finding concerns input-axis realization rather than a competing output rule. [probe.py](checks/audit/76c3f9d7128a/probe.py) is a read-only reproducer. Suggested repair: honor the full numeric override ranges independently of band defaults; implement the advertised palette/texture behavior, or explicitly retire those inert declarations.

**A1b — Additional rule-domain observation; no crash claim.** The explicitly declared `texture=all_same_sig` yields three pairs of identical horizontal length-3 signatures and zero unique signatures, yet `self_check` accepts it. This contradicts the stated unique-odd-signature invariant, and the code comment incorrectly predicts that the first pair wins. The selected Racket authority instead returns `[[8]]`, valid according to its runtime. This is recorded in [degenerate_probe.json](checks/audit/76c3f9d7128a/degenerate_probe.json) and [degenerate_racket_replay.json](checks/audit/76c3f9d7128a/degenerate_racket_replay.json); it is a domain/validator question, not evidence that ordinary sampling crashes. Consider rejecting this declared negative texture or documenting its intended authority behavior.

All bounded checks used the unchanged assigned source. No target generator, tests, reference rule, shared source, solve workspace or assignment was modified. No private labels were consulted. [commands.json](checks/audit/76c3f9d7128a/commands.json) records the exact successful verification commands and a recovered output-path collision (exit 1) separately from semantic results.
